IBM.rationale: IBM's fundamental trajectory has been severely impaired by the Q2 2026 preliminary earnings miss — the worst single-day decline in IBM's 115-year history, with the stock plunging ~25% on July 14-15. The miss exposed a critical structural vulnerability: software growth halved from 11% to ~5% in one quarter as enterprise clients aggressively reprioritized capex from software toward AI hardware (servers, storage, memory). This is not a minor miss — it directly undermines the core thesis that IBM is transforming into a high-growth software/AI platform. The Q1 2026 fundamentals that looked encouraging (revenue +9.5% YoY, EPS +14.3% YoY, OCF +18.3% YoY) are now overshadowed by the Q2 deceleration. Valuation at ~19x PE appears cheap on the surface, but this is a value trap if the software growth thesis is broken — the PE is low because the market is correctly repricing lower growth expectations. The QoQ earnings volatility (Q1 EPS of $1.28 vs Q2 2025's $2.31, a -44.6% decline) combined with the Q2 preliminary miss suggests earnings instability, not a durable franchise. The Starbucks sovereign-AI example signals structural risk that large enterprises may internalize AI capabilities, reducing third-party vendor spend. While management characterized demand as 'deferred, not lost,' the magnitude of the miss and the software growth halving represent a fundamental re-rating event, not a temporary blip. The near-term catalyst is entirely negative — the Q2 miss and guidance revision to 4%-5% revenue growth (down from 'above 5%') create a de-rating risk, not a re-rating opportunity. The stock is at 52-week lows ($204.44 intraday on July 16) with persistent selling pressure (-34% from peak), and there is no credible near-term positive catalyst to reverse the trajectory. The combination of deteriorating software growth, structural competitive threats from hyperscalers, and a broken growth narrative makes IBM extremely unattractive at this juncture.

Stock at 52-week low of $204.44 (intraday July 16), down -34% from 52-week high of $332.46, with persistent quarterly selling pressure (-19.3% and -10.5% quarterly deltas)
